question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: Sum of number_of_motorist_killed per crash_date calendar year
options.reason: Annual death counts give a direct and readily interpretable measure of the motorist fatal burden recorded in the crash file.
options.answer: This data cannot establish whether deaths per mile declined; its annual count of recorded motorist deaths was 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This data cannot answer the per-mile question because it contains no miles-driven denominator; the chart instead sums number_of_motorist_killed across police-reported NYC crash rows for each crash_date calendar year from 2013 through 2025, with no denominator. Annual counts are a defensible description of the fatal burden recorded in this dataset, and the plotted count is 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025, with substantial variation between those years. The measure leaves unanswered whether the risk per mile changed. The check covered 2,132,218 rows, found 0 missing crash dates or motorist-death values among the selected rows and all 13 years complete, so all selected rows were retained.

options.denominator: All police-reported NYC crash rows dated in the same calendar year
options.reason: Deaths per reported crash adjusts the annual death count for changes in the number of crash records.
options.answer: This data cannot establish whether deaths per mile declined; recorded motorist deaths per police-reported crash row were 0.000540 in 2013 and 0.000947 in 2025.
